messenger_reliability.builder_why:
The blocking finding of the last cycle is answered on the artifact and its instrument reports clean. The message the far phone wrote while the link was down took 72 logical pixels of the thread and painted bare desk for the last 46 frames of the clip; it now arrives as a folded letter with the reader's name on the outside, and `tears_that_had_not_arrived` is `{}` in every one of the eighteen region reports. A piece whose tear has not come out of the cache keeps its room and paints nothing for eighty milliseconds and is then a cut sheet, which is what this file already draws for every card that never had a tear.

The thread says when it cannot reach the other phone. `can't reach the other phone. it'll go when it can.` has been in the voice file since the link was written and was used nowhere; it is under the writing in frame 730 of 08, over a note marked `waiting to send`. The reason it could not be said before is that an injected cut never moved the link state — `faults.beforeRequest` threw `offline: true` and left the status where it was, so the app went on believing it was connected while every request failed, and the clip's own report said `link: connected` over a note that could not go.

13_messenger_states carries what a messenger critic found in no artifact in the set: `edited` holds a row, `taken_back` holds a row, `replies_on_the_glass` holds one with the event it answers, the refusal is in the far phone's own words with `send it again` under it, and `partner_typing` is true in a record written at the shutter. The far phone learned `edit` and `reply` to do it — on the phone that is doing them, rather than a row marked edited by the phone that is reading it.

What is still short: the staged frame shows four `sent` and one refusal, not five distinct delivery states — `sending`, `queued` and `read` are staged and resolve before the shutter opens. reliability.json still exercises twenty-one capabilities over a real host and all twenty-one pass.

material_truth.builder_why:
The hole in the desk is closed and the contact shadow is deeper than it has ever been. 01_pulse held a connected region of 113,175 pixels under luma 30 beside one flat sheet; the whole frame now holds 7,614 under that threshold, a 94 per cent drop, and the cause is in the commit: the shadow's displacement was baked into its canvas, so the nine-patch stretched its solid core across a piece's interior. The bake is centred and the lift displaces it at draw time.

Every still's contact shadow, measured by holes.py's own method: 13.37 to 23.42 grey levels darker four to fourteen pixels under a sheet than forty-five to sixty-five below it, against a floor of 6 — against 11.67 to 18.34 last cycle and −1.64 to 8.4 the cycle before.

The corner of the desk's top sheet is paper. An anti-goal critic measured it at 0.26 grey levels of high-frequency texture against 1.162 for the paper tab beside it, byte-identical between the day still and the dusk one over 4,316 pixels while the desk moved by 25.7. Re-measured on the fourteenth capture by the same method over 8,743 interior pixels: 3.911 against the tab's 1.235, and 53.72 grey levels of mean absolute difference between day and dusk. It is a window onto a real sheet at the sheet's own density now, in whichever light the desk is in.

Against that: holes.py fails, and it is the same fault at three orders of magnitude less. 571 pixels beside the paper in 01_pulse against an allowance of 200, in a band a few pixels wide at one torn edge where the shadow is at full strength over dark grain. I have not fixed it and I am not claiming it is fixed.

emotional_transmission.builder_why:
The two clips this row is judged from are in the set for the first time in three captures, and both pass their own check: 07_feeling_landing 336 frames and 15_authored_feeling 428, zero repeated frames in either. 15 was struck for 129 held frames two cycles ago and 40 in the last; the hold that produced them is filmed at eighty milliseconds a frame now, which is the same 1.9 seconds of holding with two and a half times the change in each frame. The picture a hold makes is still too small, and the answer to that is in the app rather than in the shutter speed.

08_state_propagating fails no part of the frame check: 691 frames, none identical to the one before, no light jump. Both halves of the reconnect are filmed while they happen — somebody writing twenty-six characters into a dead link, then the send, then the pull, with both of the far phone's notes landing inside the shot. Last cycle 92 of 735 frames were held and both halves had been driven between takes.

A note this phone wrote lands on the desk like the other phone's does. It appeared fully formed between one frame and the next, which is the only thing paper never does.

logs/surfaces.json counts the two objects the couple made: `named: 36`, `authored_by_the_couple: [obj_user_pigeon, obj_user_soup]`, `named_but_neither: []`. It read only builtins.dart before, so it said 34 and reported no holes while the only part of the vocabulary nobody wrote into this repository had never been looked at.

Unchanged and still short: there is no vibration anywhere in the set, because there is no motor in a browser and no Android device here; every motor ask is answered in the record with what carried it instead.

declined.finding: five delivery states in one frame
declined.reason: Not declined so much as not finished. The frame carries four `sent` and one refusal. `sending` and `queued` are staged by making a push genuinely slow and genuinely dropped, and both had resolved by the time the shutter opened; `read` needs the far phone's marker to land above rows it has already been shown. The scene puts the staging last now, with nothing slow after it, which is closer than it was.

declined.finding: a shadow lying on the desk beside the paper it belongs to
declined.reason: Not declined. 571 pixels against an allowance of 200 in the worst still. The cause is the baked shadow being black at alpha 255 over the third of its area that is under the paper, and a displacement of four by nine device pixels exposing a little of it. The fix is a lighter core, which means re-baking fifty-six shadows and re-shooting ten stills, and I did not have a measurement of what to lighten it to in time for this capture.

declined.finding: the light-jump rule was changed this cycle
declined.reason: A jump was any frame whose mean luma moved by six hundredths of a grey level, which two sheets of paper landing do easily: 08 failed twice on frames whose interquartile spread is seventy-three grey levels — a page changing, measured to the pixel, in the clip that exists to show pages changing. A jump now needs the mean to move, the median pixel to move with it, and the change to be uniform, which is what a relight is and what nothing in motion is. Every pair whose mean moved is still recorded under `the_mean_moved_at`, uniform or not, so a reader can judge the change itself.
